The Greek advanced in many days is rendered jointly as was of a great age. The participle contributes the attained advanced state, en locates that advancement in days, and many specifies their extent; English recasts these as a state of great age. Splitting many onto great is plausible, but great also carries the advancement that was of an age alone does not express, so that allocation is not independently preferable. Retain the noncompositional phrase, headed on the participle and the lexical age anchor.
